info.name: NIDP — DaaS + Query API
info.description:
## How to use this collection

1. **Get an API key** — provisioned by Nivesh ops via
   `POST /admin/keys` (which itself needs `NIDP_DAAS_INTERNAL_TOKEN`).
   The key looks like `nvd_...`.
2. **Set the `NIDP_API_KEY` collection variable** — Collection → Variables →
   paste the `nvd_...` token into *Current Value*.
3. **(Optional) `NIDP_INTERNAL_TOKEN`** — only needed for the 3
   `/admin/keys` endpoints; paste the `NIDP_DAAS_INTERNAL_TOKEN` value.
4. **(Optional) switch service** — change `BASE_URL` to:
   - DaaS  : `https://data.niveshcopilot.com/daas`  (default)
   - Query : `https://data.niveshcopilot.com/query`

`/v1/*` requests inherit `X-API-Key: {{NIDP_API_KEY}}`. `/admin/keys/*`
requests override with `Authorization: Bearer {{NIDP_INTERNAL_TOKEN}}`.
Public probes (`/health`, `/openapi.json`) inherit but are ignored
server-side.


---

Consolidated OpenAPI specification for all NIDP services.

## Services

| Service | Base URL | Audience |
|---------|----------|----------|
| **DaaS API** | `https://data.niveshcopilot.com/daas` | Partner/client — API key required |
| **Query API** | `https://data.niveshcopilot.com/query` | Internal — Bearer token |

## DaaS Authentication

Every `/v1/*` endpoint requires an API key issued by Nivesh ops:

```
X-API-Key: nvd_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
# or
Authorization: Bearer nvd_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

`/admin/*` endpoints require the internal `NIDP_DAAS_INTERNAL_TOKEN` Bearer token.

## Query API Authentication

All Query endpoints require:

```
Authorization: Bearer <NIDP_QUERY_API_TOKEN>
```

## Rate Limits (DaaS)

Each key has a per-minute RPM cap and a daily quota. Every response includes:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `X-RateLimit-Remaining` / `X-RateLimit-Reset`
- `X-Daily-Limit` / `X-Daily-Remaining`

A 429 response includes a `Retry-After` header.

## Pagination (DaaS)

List endpoints accept `limit` (1–5000, default 100) and `offset`.
Response envelopes include `pagination.next_offset` when more rows are available.

## Conventions

- Dates: `YYYY-MM-DD`; timestamps: ISO 8601 UTC
- Symbols: canonical NSE tickers, upper-cased server-side
- Numeric values decoded from `NUMERIC` to JSON numbers

request.description:
Top-N schemes within a category

Category leaderboard sorted by selected metric.

Category leaderboard with composite scores

Full scorecard leaderboard for a sub-category, sorted by composite score
or any individual metric.  Includes quality labels and quartile flags.

Full category scorecard for a scheme

Returns composite score, quality label, per-metric ranks and quartiles
within the fund's sub-category peer group.

Consumes nidp.v_mf_category_scorecard (migration 052), which joins
analytics.fund_category_rank + mf_derived_analytics + disclosure snapshots
+ holdings to produce 73 columns including:
  - composite_score (0–100), quality_label (Elite … Underperformer)
  - composite_rank, total_in_category, top_position_pct
  - rank_ret1y / rank_ret3y / rank_ret5y / rank_sharpe / rank_ter / …
  - qtile_ret1y / qtile_sharpe / qtile_maxdd / qtile_ter / … (1=Q1 best)
  - pct_ret1y / pct_sharpe / … (0–1 PERCENT_RANK for radar charts)

Composite-score-filtered MF screener

Advanced MF screener driven by nidp.v_mf_category_scorecard (migration 052).

Every returned scheme has composite_score, quality_label, and quartile ranks.
Combines well with the MF intelligence tool in the copilot.

Top funds across all categories by a single metric

Cross-category top-fund screener.

Performance metrics for a single scheme

Returns the latest computed return + risk metrics for a scheme.

Bulk V3 MF primitives by ISIN

Return the V3 primitive row for each requested ISIN, keyed by
ISIN in the response.

The natural cross-system identifier for Indian mutual funds. CAS
imports populate ISIN per holding by construction, and the NIDP
side stores both Growth and IDCW ISIN variants. The view (migration
058) emits one row per (scheme_code, ISIN) so each variant has its
own primitive bundle.

Missing ISINs are simply absent from the response — callers should
degrade gracefully when a fund has no V3 primitives.

Bulk latest V3 MF scores by ISIN

Returns the latest persisted score per requested ISIN, keyed by ISIN.

Missing ISINs are simply absent from the response — callers should degrade
gracefully when a fund has no persisted score (e.g., new scheme that the
nightly engine hasn't covered yet).

AMC master list with scheme counts

All mutual fund AMCs tracked in the warehouse, ordered by AUM descending.

AMFI notices, circulars, and addenda

AMFI-published lifecycle documents. Source for scheme mergers, renames, regulatory changes.

Catalog

Feeds

Per-ingester health view. Three enhancements over a plain
v_feed_status read:

  1. effective_last_success_at = COALESCE(source_registry, max(job_log.started_at)
     WHERE status='OK'). The ingester upsert doesn't always update
     source_registry.last_success_at, so falling back to job_log
     keeps the column populated.
  2. last_7_days = [{date, status}] for the trailing week, derived
     from job_log. Drives the dashboard's mini week-strip widget.
  3. Sort by last_run_at DESC NULLS LAST — most-active feeds at top,
     dormant/never-run feeds at the bottom.

Feed Calendar

Per-day status for the last N days, derived from job_log. One
cell per calendar day. Useful for the Console's week-strip widget.

Status priority within a day (worst wins): FAILED > PARTIAL > OK >
SKIPPED. Days with no runs return status=null.

Feed Log Path

Return the on-disk log path for the ingester (exists or not).
Convenience for ops who want to ssh in and tail manually.

Feed Logs

Tail the last N lines of the ingester's VM log file.

Returns 404 with a clear message if the log doesn't exist yet
(service has never run on this VM).

Feed Execute

Spawn run_service.sh <ingester> [--date YYYY-MM-DD] in the
background. Returns 202 immediately; UI polls
/feeds/{ingester}/runs to see results land in nidp.job_log when
the job completes.

On VMs run_service.sh is used (handles flock, logging, venv).
In Docker/dev environments it falls back to spawning the current
Python interpreter directly so the sync works without the VM wrapper.

request.description:
Multi-metric stock screener from NIDP feature store

Screener over the NIDP stock feature store. Returns raw V3 primitives
for qualifying stocks, sorted by the chosen metric. The copilot uses this
to generate quality-ranked or momentum-ranked pick lists.

Top-N stocks by a single metric

Top-N stocks by a chosen metric (quality, momentum, return, etc.)
Used by the copilot recommendation node for sector-specific or universe-wide picks.

Full V3 primitive row for one stock

Returns the full set of V3 scoring primitives for a stock from the NIDP
feature store. The copilot uses these to compute composite scores and build
a multi-dimension analysis.
Bulk latest V3 stock scores by symbol

Bulk V3 stock primitives by NSE symbol

Return the latest V3 primitive row for each requested symbol,
keyed by symbol in the response.

Saves N HTTP round-trips vs ``GET /v1/stocks/{symbol}/score`` when
the V3 engine enriches an entire portfolio in one shot. The Nivesh-side
``services/portfolio_enrichment.py`` calls this endpoint instead of
reading ``nidp.v_v3_stock_primitives`` over the shared PG pool.
